subject: Audit traceability, telemetry retention, and fault-containment RFI
messages:
From: Asha Menon <asha.menon@halcyonfin.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.example.com
Cc: procure@halcyonfin.com
Date: 2028-03-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFI: audit traceability, telemetry retention & fault containment

Aditya,

Thanks for picking this up. As part of Halcyon Financial's vendor security review we need a concise RFI that covers three areas: control-plane / data-plane fault containment, telemetry and audit traceability (forensics), and retention/archival policies. Attached is our short questionnaire (Halcyon_RFI_Questionnaire.xlsx) — we've highlighted the sections we want prioritized. Key asks: 

- A network/topology diagram showing control/data path separation and where tenant traffic terminates.
- What artifacts are retained per inference request (metadata, client IP, request payload, model id, response hashes) and retention periods.
- The timeline and fidelity at which you can reconstruct a single inference request for audit (what logs, order of events, guaranteed fields).
- How you isolate failure domains to prevent cross-tenant lateral impact (example: a control-plane mailbox outage, GPU pool flapping).

We are aiming to complete vendor evaluations by 2028-03-30. Can you confirm if you can provide the requested diagram and a short summary (1-2 pages) by EOD 2028-03-22? Also note any available artifacts (SOC 2 Type II, penetration test summary) and delivery method (secure link, redacted PDF).

Appreciate it — if it's easier we can schedule a 30-min call to walk through details.

Regards,
Asha Menon
Security Architect, Vendor Risk
Halcyon Financial
asha.menon@halcyonfin.com
+1 (415) 555-0148

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha.menon@halcyonfin.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-03-21T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: audit traceability, telemetry retention & fault containment

Asha —

Thanks for the clear list. We can hit EOD 2028-03-22 for the deliverables you requested. I've attached: redwood_topology_diagram_v3.png (annotated control/data demarcation), and telemetry_retention_matrix.pdf (per-artifact retention and retention justification). High-level summary below — we'll include this and a short packet in the Drive link by tomorrow.

1) Control / data separation (summary):
- Control plane (orchestration, model management, routing) runs in a logically separated management plane; customer workloads are executed in tenant-bound inference pools.
- Tenant inference traffic terminates on tenant-dedicated or logically isolated GPU pools depending on the plan (Dedicated vs Hosted w/ soft tenancy).
- Network enforcement: namespace-level firewalling + ephemeral sidecar proxies enforce strict egress allowlists. The diagram shows the control-plane endpoints (api.redwood.internal), model artifact store (S3-mux), and tenant execution plane with sidecar boundary.

2) Retained artifacts per request (short):
- Request metadata (timestamp, model_id, model_version, request_id, route_id) — retained for 90 days by default; configurable to 365 days for enterprise contracts.
- Request headers (client IP as hashed + salt by default; optional raw IP retention under NDA) — hashed IP stored for 90 days.
- Input payloads: default sampling/none depending on plan; for audit we can enable full plaintext retention into an encrypted S3 bucket for a customer-specific retention window.
- Response hashes and debug token (opaque id for reconstruction) — stored for 365 days.
- Operational traces (k8s events, runtime logs, GPU job metadata) — retained 30 days; aggregated traces pushed to long-term archive on request.

3) Forensic reconstruction capability:
- We can reconstruct an individual inference invocation if either (a) request_id or (b) response_hash is provided plus a time range. Reconstruction fidelity varies with plan and retention config. Typical reconstruction timeline: index lookup -> trace aggregation (0-5 mins) -> artifact retrieval (up to 1 hour for archived S3 retrieval if cold). Guaranteed minimal fields: request_id, model_id, model_version, routing_node_id, timestamp.

4) Failure containment and blast radius:
- GPU pools are grouped into fault-domains; control plane provides automated fallback to other pools with cross-pool scaling disabled by default for Dedicated tenants.
- Sidecar-level rate limits and token buckets prevent noisy-tenant saturation; circuit-breakers trigger automatic shed policies.
- Control plane outages degrade management actions (rollouts) but not in-flight inference for Dedicated pools; Hosted plans may fall back to a lower-throughput path with degraded latency.

Attachments and artifacts: SOC2_TypeII_redacted.pdf can be delivered via a secure Drive link (we'll provide a redacted copy). For the topology we included an annotated PNG.

Next steps: I'll drop the Drive link and a 2-page summary into the Halcyon folder by 10:00 PT tomorrow. If you'd like a call, Sergio (cc'ed) can join to walk technical details about trace artifacts.

Best,

--
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Security Integrations
Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.example.com
+1 (650) 555-0210

From: Asha Menon <asha.menon@halcyonfin.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.example.com
Cc: procure@halcyonfin.com
Date: 2028-03-22T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: audit traceability, telemetry retention & fault containment

Aditya —

Thanks for the prompt response and the attachments so far. A couple of clarifying items before we finalize: 

- When you say client IPs are hashed+salted, can you confirm the hashing algorithm and whether salts are per-tenant or global? Halcyon policy requires per-tenant salt for user privacy.
- For the reconstruction window: if an archived payload needs retrieval, you note up to 1 hour — can you provide SLA for retrieval (e.g., within 60 min for enterprise customers) and whether that includes decryption step?
- Regarding forensic minimal fields: is model_version immutable (i.e., do you keep model version history for each inference) or do rollouts map old request_ids to new model versions?
- Finally, can you share a redacted SOC2 Type II and a short penetration test executive summary (we accept redacted copies over secure link).

Also copying our procurement team with an expected procurement timeline.

Asha

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>

Date: 2028-03-23T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: audit traceability, telemetry retention & fault containment

Hi Asha —

Following up with the concrete items and process notes so procurement has what they need: 

1) SOC2 and PenTest: we've uploaded a redacted SOC2 Type II to the secure folder and a short penetration-test executive summary. Link: https://drive.redwood.example.com/s/halcyon-evidence-2028 (link included in the RFI package). For anything that requires an NDA prior to delivery, please reply with the procurement contact and we will route through legal.

2) Salt / IP hashing: technical answer below (Sergio please confirm via reply): we use HMAC-SHA256 with a per-tenant salt stored in the KMS-backed secrets store; salts are rotated quarterly on enterprise contracts. If Halcyon requires a different cadence or salt control model we can accommodate under a custom contract.

3) Archive retrieval SLA: enterprise retrieval (cold S3 archive -> hot access) is 60 minutes RTO for retained inference payloads when the retention policy is set to "enterprise-audit" in the contract. Decryption is factored into that SLA as our KMS steps are included.

4) Model versioning: model_version is immutable for stored request artifacts; rollouts create new model_version identifiers and we keep mapping tables for 24 months by default (configurable). Historical requests map to the model_version present at time of invocation.

Procurement: Marissa here — attaching a draft MOU and a statement of work to accelerate contracting. If Halcyon is happy with the technical answers we'll prepare a standard enterprise addendum that includes the telemetry retention window and the retrieval SLA. DocuSign draft: https://docusign.com/doc/ABC1234

Please confirm receipt and whether you want a technical call. Sergio (cc) will provide any additional evidence or clarifications on trace fields.

Thanks,
